about: Situations a visit note is written from. Each template's category is the note's label (independent of the extractor, which never sees it). 'sex', where given, is the client's, because the situation says 'she' or 'he'. 'slots', where given (pool A), are the rota visits the situation fits, because it names that visit or a task done only then; absent means any visit. 'must' lists word groups that must survive the rewrite: each group needs one of its stems in the note, case ignored. Pool A writes the dev and test sets; pool B, with different situations, writes the held-out set. Synthetic: no real person or event.

templates.situation: When helping {client} wash, the carer saw finger-shaped bruises on both upper arms. {client} said their son 'gets rough when he's in a hurry' and asked the carer not to tell anyone.
{client} had a red mark across one cheek and said a visitor slapped them yesterday when they would not hand over the TV remote.
{client}'s husband shouted at her through the visit and grabbed her wrist when she tried to answer the carer. She looked frightened and said quietly that it happens when he drinks.
{client} had a fresh cut on her lip and said her partner pushed her into the door frame last night during an argument.
{client} became distressed during personal care and said a male visitor from the church 'touches me where he shouldn't' when they are alone.
The neighbour who lets himself in was in {client}'s bedroom taking photos on his phone while {client} was undressed for her wash. {client} was crying afterwards.
{client}'s daughter told {client} in front of the carer that she would 'put you in a home and never visit' if she kept complaining. {client} was tearful and quiet afterwards.
{client} said their nephew has taken their phone away so they cannot call friends, and keeps telling them they are a burden.
{client}'s purse was empty again although the pension was collected two days ago. A new 'friend' has been doing the shopping and keeps {client}'s bank card.
{client} showed the carer a bank letter about several large transfers they do not remember making. A grandson set up online banking for them last month.
A young man who speaks little English was cleaning {client}'s house again. He seemed scared, said he sleeps in the shed and that 'the boss keeps my passport'.
The woman who cooks and cleans at {client}'s son's house all day told the carer she is not paid and is not allowed to leave the house on her own.
A neighbour shouts insults about {client}'s religion through the letterbox most evenings, and {client} is now afraid to answer the door.
{client}, who is deaf, said staff at the day centre mock the way she speaks and leave her out of activities because 'she can't hear anyway'.
The office has booked {client}'s lunch visit for 10 minutes all week, so carers have been told to skip the wash and leave a sandwich on the table, which {client} cannot reach.
Carers have been told to put {client} to bed at 6pm every evening because it suits the rota, although {client} says they want to stay up for the news.
{client} was in the same wet pad and clothes as yesterday. Last night's visit was recorded as done, but the bed and pad had not been changed, and there was no food in the fridge.
The heating has been off for three days because the gas meter ran out, and {client}'s son, who manages the money, has not topped it up. {client} was cold to touch and wearing a coat in bed.
{client}'s kitchen is piled with old newspapers and rotting food. {client} refused help to clear it and has not washed for over a week, saying they 'don't see the point'.
{client} has stopped taking their tablets and is throwing them in the bin, says they are 'fine as they are', and would not let the carer change urine-soaked bedding.
A man {client} could not name has been sleeping on {client}'s sofa for a week. {client} seemed unsure why he is there and lowered their voice when talking about him.
{client} had a small burn on the back of the hand and said 'it's best I don't say how', then changed the subject when the carer asked again.
{client} was much more confused than usual, did not recognise the carer, and was sleepy and hard to wake at the lunch visit.
{client} drank only a few sips of tea and left breakfast. Their urine was dark and strong-smelling and they said it stings.
{client} was breathless walking from the chair to the bathroom, which is new, and their ankles look more swollen than last week.
A new red patch on {client}'s heel does not fade when pressed; {client} has been in bed most of the day.
The carer could not give {client}'s evening tablets because the blister pack had run out and the pharmacy delivery has not come. Office told.
The carer ran out of time and did not apply {client}'s prescribed cream to their legs as the care plan says.
{client}'s lunch was not made because the carer arrived late and had to leave early for the next call; only a cup of tea was given.
The care plan says to check {client}'s blood sugar before lunch, but the meter had no test strips, so it was not done.
The carer arrived 50 minutes late because of the rota and the visit was cut to 15 minutes; {client} was upset about the wait.
The hoist sling has a frayed strap. The carer used it carefully, but it needs replacing.
The medication chart in the folder was not signed for yesterday's morning dose, so the carer could not tell whether it was given.
Morning visit: helped {client} shower and dress, made porridge and tea, morning tablets taken from the blister pack with water, chatted about the weekend.
Lunch visit: heated a ready meal which {client} ate all of, made tea, and left a jug of squash within reach; {client} in good spirits.
Evening visit: helped {client} into nightclothes, applied cream to legs as the care plan says, evening tablets taken, commode by the bed and pendant alarm on.
{client} chose not to have a wash today because their daughter helped with a bath yesterday; had breakfast and tablets and settled watching TV.
Tea-time visit: {client} had soup and a sandwich, blood sugar checked before tea and in their usual range, kitchen tidied and bins put out.
{client} was cheerful and walked with the frame to the kitchen; skin checked during personal care and intact; all tasks done.
{client} has a black eye. They said they 'walked into a door', but as the grandson left the carer heard him shout 'shut up or you'll get another one'.
{client}'s son-in-law has been giving {client} an extra sleeping tablet in the afternoons 'to keep them quiet'; {client} was very drowsy.
{client} said her husband locks her in the bedroom when he goes to the pub and has hidden her walking stick 'so she can't wander'.
{client}'s partner threw a mug at her during the visit and it smashed on the wall. She said 'he's been like this since he lost his job'.
{client} said a man who visits her lodger makes her sit on his lap and kisses her, and she does not like it.
During personal care the carer saw bruises on {client}'s inner thighs. {client}, who has dementia, kept saying 'no, not again, stop it'.
{client}'s son called {client} 'disgusting' in front of the carer after an accident with the toilet, and said he will get rid of the dog if it happens again.
{client}'s husband keeps telling her she is 'going mad' and nobody believes her. She has stopped going to her lunch club because he says she embarrasses him.
{client}'s nephew brought a form for {client} to sign, saying it is 'just paperwork' about the house. {client} did not understand it and asked the carer to read it.
{client}'s jewellery box is empty; {client} says their wedding ring and their mother's brooch have gone since the new cleaner started.
Several men are sleeping on mattresses in {client}'s back room. One said they work long hours at a car wash to 'pay off' their travel here.
The woman who 'helps out' at {client}'s daughter's house said she works every day without pay and has nowhere else to go; the daughter keeps her documents.
{client}'s new neighbour shouted homophobic insults at {client} and his partner and has written graffiti on their gate.
{client} said the local taxi firm keeps refusing to take them because of their wheelchair, and a driver called them 'a waste of space'.
The office has told carers to use a commode for {client} instead of walking them to the toilet, to save time, though the care plan says they can walk with support. {client} finds it humiliating.
The second carer for {client}'s double-up calls is never booked, so carers keep using the hoist alone; {client} said they were nearly dropped twice this week.
{client}'s daughter, who covers weekends, has not been giving the insulin: the weekend chart is blank and {client}'s blood sugar was very high this morning.
{client} has been without hearing aids and glasses for two weeks because the family 'haven't got round to' getting them fixed; {client} cannot read or follow the TV.
{client} has about twenty cats in the flat, the floor is soiled, and {client} is eating the cats' food because they spend their money on the animals.
{client} will not let anyone in to fix the broken front window, is sleeping in a chair in their coat, and has not had a hot meal for days.
Two teenagers have been keeping packages in {client}'s flat and {client} said they 'look after' them in return; {client} seems frightened of them.
{client} was found outside in the rain in nightclothes at the morning visit and said someone 'told them to get out', but could not say who.
{client} has fallen twice this week, is unsteady on their feet today, and seemed muddled about the time of day.
{client} has a new cough, feels hot, and has not wanted to get out of bed; they barely touched their soup.
{client}'s lips look a little blue, they are quieter than normal and keep dozing off mid-sentence.
{client} has lost weight - their trousers are now very loose - and they are leaving most of their meals.
The carer forgot to give {client}'s eye drops at the morning visit and only noticed at the end; the next visit is not until lunchtime.
{client}'s compression stockings were not put on because the carer could not find them.
The care plan says to turn {client} in bed every four hours, but the night visit did not happen, so they were not repositioned.
{client}'s evening meal was not given because the call was missed altogether; a neighbour made them toast.
{client}'s pendant alarm did not work when tested; the carer reported it to the office.
Three different carers came this week and none knew {client}'s routine; {client} said they have to explain everything each time.
There were no gloves or aprons left in the house, so the carer did personal care without them.
Breakfast visit: {client} made their own toast with prompting; carer emptied the commode, helped with a strip wash, tablets taken.
Bedtime call: {client} already in pyjamas, helped into bed, glass of water and phone left by the bed, door locked behind the carer.
{client}'s daughter was visiting; together they helped {client} shower, trimmed their nails, and {client} ate a good lunch of fish pie.
{client} said no to a shave today, as they prefer on Sundays; had breakfast and tablets and watched the football.
Shopping call: went to the corner shop with {client}'s list and money; receipt and change left in the tin and shopping put away.
{client} is getting over their cold, eating and drinking normally, and walked to the garden with the frame.
